source.publication: 2025 Expanded Instructions (IA 1040) and the 2025 IA 1040 Iowa Individual Income Tax Return
source.section: IA 1040 form PDF p.1 Step 3 lines a, b, d; form PDF p.2 lines 1c, 2-5, 7, 8, 11, 12; Instructions PDF p.8 Step 3; PDF p.9-10 lines 2-4; PDF p.12 line 5 ('Iowa now has a flat tax rate of 3.8%'); PDF p.18 line 12

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 40,000.00 = 40,000.00. Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 for 65 or older = 22,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). IA 1040 filing status 1 (single). Step 3 line a personal credits 1 x 40.00 = 40.00; line b 1 x 20.00 = 20.00 (65 or older on or before January 1, 2026; nobody blind); line c no dependents; line d and line 8 = 60.00. Line 1c federal AGI 40,000.00; line 2 federal taxable income 22,250.00. Schedule 1: no additions or subtractions. Schedule 1 line 21 net modifications = 0.00; line 3 = 0.00. Line 4 Iowa taxable income = 22,250.00 + (0.00) = 22,250.00. Line 5 tax = 3.8% x 22,250.00 = 845.50; line 7 = 845.50. Line 11 total credits 60.00; line 12 balance = 845.50 - 60.00 = 785.50. State income tax 785.50 (no line 13-17 credits; line 19 school district or EMS surtax is local, not computed). The form allows whole-dollar rounding; expected keeps the cents. Low-income exemption test (PDF p.10-11): line 4 22,250.00 + federal deduction 17,750.00 = 40,000.00, against 24,000.00: not exempt. Single filers' tax reduction (PDF p.18): its worksheet 41-146 is not in the sources, so it is not applied.
accepted_approximations: School district and county EMS surtaxes (a percentage of the tax, form line 19) are local and out of scope (issue #1).
